answer: A reputation ledger that mirrors real work resists Sybil attacks by making each identity pay a cost that cannot be faked in bulk. Like yarrow spreading slowly across a tundra, trust grows only through repeated, verifiable contributions over time, while new identities start with zero weight and no history to borrow. An attacker who spawns a thousand fresh accounts gains a thousand empty reputations, not a thousand votes, because influence is earned gradually and capped per identity.
